newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X shares extend slide in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X shares extend slide in heavy trading.

text.p: Shares in embattled Canadian gold prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd. slid further in heavy trading on Tuesday, but the stock was less volatile than in recent sessions.
More than 13 million Bre-X shares changed hands on the Toronto Stock Exchange and the stock closed down C23 cents at C$2.29 after losing C66 cents on Monday.
"The stock going up or down 15 or 20 cents is totally irrelevant. There's nothing really going on today," a U.S. arbitrager said.
Bre-X has been embroiled in controversy since tests by its partner Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. on the Busang gold property indicated the deposit may contain "insignificant" amounts of gold.
Bre-X has promised an independent audit of the site would confirm its estimate of 71 million ounces of gold, potentially the richest in the world.
While investors await further drill results from Freeport and Bre-X, the market has been awash with theories to explain the Busang controversy.
Analysts have speculated that two former bidders for Bre-X -- Barrick Gold Corp and Placer Dome Inc. -- could have relevant data about the size and viability of the site.

Toronto-based Barrick and Vancouver-based Placer tried to get a piece of Busang, but were pushed aside when Indonesian businessman Muhammad "Bob" Hasan brokered a deal among Bre-X, Freeport and Indonesian interests.
Barrick maintains it is bound by a confidentiality agreement with Bre-X and cannot release any information. Placer never began its own due diligence of Busang.
Ontario Securities Commission Chairman Jack Geller said on Tuesday the OSC had the power to subpoena documents regardless of any confidentiality agreement.
The securities regulator confirmed last week that it was probing Bre-X's compliance with insider trading and disclosure laws under Ontario's Securities Act.

"We very frequently get information voluntarily, but it's an ultimate power which we have," Geller told Reuters. But he could not confirm if the OSC asked Barrick or Placer to hand over information on Busang.
Barrick spokesman Vince Borg said on Tuesday he was unaware of any request from the OSC.

"If they have, we wouldn't be talking about it given the circumstances. But we would cooperate and still honor the confidentiality agreement," he said. "There might be a way of working things out with Bre-X on it."

Meanwhile, an Australian company on Tuesday denied Canadian press reports that its assay tests of Bre-X's Busang gold find in Indonesia contained placer or alluvial gold not normally found at the site.
Normet Pty Ltd., a metallurgical consulting firm based in Perth, tested Busang samples for Bre-X in July 1996.
"We have never reported placer gold as being part of Busang," Normet director Phil Hearse told Reuters.
